title: Physical vs. Chemical Changes
ques: Tearing a piece of paper into tiny pieces is one type of change, and burning that paper into ashes is another. Which one is a physical change and which one is a chemical change?

answer.content:
*   **Tearing the paper** is a **Physical Change**, because it is still paper, just in smaller pieces.
*   **Burning the paper** is a **Chemical Change**, because it turns into a completely new substance (ash and smoke) and cannot be turned back into paper.

explanation: This exercise clarifies the fundamental distinction between changing form and changing chemical identity.

title: Reversible Changes
ques: Give an example of a change involving water that is completely reversible (meaning you can easily change it back to how it was).

answer.content: An example is **freezing water into ice**. It is reversible because if you take the ice out of the freezer and let it warm up, it will melt back into liquid water.

explanation: This tests the concept of physical reversibility.

title: Irreversible Changes
ques: When you bake a cake in the oven, liquid batter turns into a fluffy solid. Is this change reversible or irreversible, and why?

answer.content: Baking a cake is an **Irreversible Change** (and a chemical change). Once the ingredients are baked together, you cannot separate them back into flour, eggs, and milk. The heat has permanently changed them.

explanation: This demonstrates an irreversible chemical change using a common household activity.
